Q: Rounding in the JavaScript toFixed() method A:

The problem you are encountering is not specific to JavaScript. It is common to computing in general.

Both these arithmetic calculations have the same result, 0.075:

  • 0.25 * 0.3 = 0.075
  • 0.025 * 3 = 0.075

This is using the decimal number system commonly used.

Computers, at their core, however, don't use the decimal system, but binary. Everything is based on 0 and 1.

Because of this, they actually have a hard time getting the calculation above right. JavaScript and other programming languages have to approximate the result, giving you this:

  • 0.25 * 0.3 = 0.75
  • 0.025 * 3 = 0.07500000000000001

You can now see why toFixed returns different results:

  • 0.75.toFixed(2) = 0.07
  • 0.07500000000000001.toFixed(2) = 0.08

Q: Inline and extern keyword for constants A:

I'm trying to define global constant variables that are shared across multiple source files in my project (using modern C++17 features).

For example, constants used for loop iteration counts or fixed gameplay values (such as limits or configuration values) that won't change at runtime in my game.

I want to understand whether it's better to use extern variables with a separate source file for the definition and a header file for the declaration, or to use inline variables (a C++17 feature) that can be defined directly in a header file and shared across multiple files.

When is each approach more appropriate in practice?
